{{Short description|5th-century king of Wa}}
{{Five kings of Wa}}
'''Chin of Wa''' (倭珍) was a king of [[Wa (Japan)|Wa]] in the early [[5th century]] (middle [[Kofun period|Kofun era]]). He was also known as '''Wa Ochin''' (倭王珍).{{Sfn|倭王珍（日本人名大辞典）}}

[[San of Wa|San]]'s younger brother and one of the ''[[Five kings of Wa]]''. Some compare him to the 18th [[Emperor Hanzei]].

== Records ==

=== Book of Liang ===

; [[Book of Liang]]
: In the [[Book of Liang]], the article on Japan states that after the death of the Japanese king "Zan", his younger brother "Ya" stood up, and after his death, his son "Je" stood up.<ref name="東洋文庫 梁書">『東アジア民族史 1 正史東夷伝（東洋文庫264）』 平凡社、1974年、pp. 315-319。</ref>。

=== History of the Southern Dynasties ===
In the [[History of the Southern Dynasties|Nan shi]], the article on the Japanese Kingdom (Nan shi wagu den) describes the contents of the Song Shu Chronicles.
